notice: Generated by scripts/export_contracts.py. Read-only tools Gemini can call; MCP servers asap, gscm, nerp and wizard each serve their scope, and portal serves the portal tools on a PC with company portals configured. The dashboards tools are served on a PC with a dashboards folder set. With NERP connected (Settings → NERP), nerp serves its view tools (nerp_list_views, nerp_view_columns, nerp_query) instead of its report tools.

tools.name: asap_search_reports
tools.description: Search the ASAP report catalog you are allowed to see (market share, Smart Switch, installed base, app engagement and finance reports). Returns report ids, names, folders, measures and whether rows can be read (row_access ROWS) or the report is navigation only.

query.description: Words to look for in report names, descriptions, folders and column names, e.g. 'marketing spend quarter' (1-200 characters)

tools.name: asap_get_report_schema
tools.description: Describe one ASAP report: grain, dimensions you can filter or group by, measures with units and aggregation rules, prompts, caveats, freshness and your market access.

report_id.description: Report id from a search result (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{2,79}$)

tools.name: asap_run_report
tools.description: Read rows from one ASAP report with prompt filters and optional grouping (read-only, at most 500 rows). Each call is recorded as evidence with an id such as E3: cite it as [E3] next to numbers that come from it. Missing rows mean no data, not zero.

report_id.description: Report id from a search result (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{2,79}$)

filters.description: Prompt answers: rows must match every filter.

field.description: A dimension key from the report schema, e.g. market, fiscal_quarter, month, model_code (pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$)

group_by.description: Optional dimensions to aggregate to. Omit to get rows at the report grain. Measures aggregate by their declared rule (sum, period-end balance, or not aggregatable).

measures.description: Optional subset of measure keys; omit for all.

tools.name: wizard_list_sources
tools.description: List the source systems you can use (report catalogs, the database, the portals, the team's dashboards), their data families (spend, sell-out, share, switching...), connector status and data mode (SYNTHETIC, LIVE, DATED_APPROVED_SNAPSHOT or LIVE_VERIFIED).

tools.name: wizard_search_catalog
tools.description: Search every report you can access across all systems at once. Use when you do not know which system holds the data.

query.description: Words describing the data you need, e.g. 'smart switch apple' (1-200 characters)

tools.name: wizard_lookup_definitions
tools.description: Search the company knowledge base: business definitions (sell-through, share, investment-efficiency proxy, observed switchers), fiscal calendar, markets and models, platform guides, and company notes on the organisation, products, processes and internal acronyms. Use it whenever a term, acronym, team, product or process matters to the answer. Returns the best-matching notes (long notes: the matching sections), each showing whether an owner has signed it, when an expert last confirmed it, and the mapped portal reports that measure the term (portal_reports).

query.description: Term, acronym or topic, e.g. 'sell-through', 'fiscal quarter', 'ROI', 'launch process' (1-200 characters)

tools.name: wizard_browse_knowledge
tools.description: Table of contents of the company knowledge base: every area (company, processes, glossary, metrics, platforms...) and note with a one-line summary. Use it to see what is documented, or when a search finds nothing.

area.description: Only this area (e.g. 'company', 'processes', 'glossary', 'metrics'). Omit to list every area and note (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,40}$)

tools.name: wizard_read_knowledge
tools.description: Read up to 5 knowledge notes in full by id (ids come from wizard_browse_knowledge or wizard_lookup_definitions), with their approval status, expert check, related note ids and the mapped portal reports that measure the term.

ids.description: Note ids from wizard_browse_knowledge or wizard_lookup_definitions, e.g. ['fiscal-calendar'].

tools.name: wizard_read_attachment
tools.description: Read a file the user attached to this conversation (PowerPoint, Excel, Word, email, CSV), converted to text: slides with their charts' values and notes, sheets with column profiles and formulas. Use the label listed in the request (F1, F2...). The first call lists the file's parts; read a part by name for long files. Each read is evidence (USER_PROVIDED) to cite like [E3].

file.description: The attached file's label, e.g. 'F1' (listed in the request) (pattern ^F[0-9]{1,3}$)

part.description: Only this part, e.g. 'Slide 4' or 'Sheet: Sales' (names come back in 'parts'). Omit to read from the start (0-120 characters)

offset.description: Continue a long file from the next_offset you were given (default 0)

tools.name: wizard_query_attachment
tools.description: Filter, group and total ALL rows of an attached spreadsheet or CSV (the text from wizard_read_attachment shows large sheets only as a profile). Column keys are listed in wizard_read_attachment's 'tables'. Each call is evidence (USER_PROVIDED) to cite like [E3]; never add up rates, shares or prices.

sheet.description: Sheet name; needed when the file has several (0-120 characters)

column.description: Column key from the file's table, e.g. 'market' (pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$)

values.description: Keep rows whose value is one of these (case-insensitive).

from.description: Keep rows at or above this value (numbers compare as numbers, text and dates as text) (0-40 characters)

to.description: Keep rows at or below this value (0-40 characters)

group_by.description: Column keys to group by; empty with measures gives one total row.

measures.description: Totals to compute; omit (and group_by) to get matching rows.

column.description: Number column to total (any column for count) (pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$)

aggregate.description: How to combine the rows of each group.

tools.name: wizard_edit_attachment
tools.description: Change an attached Excel workbook and give the user the edited file: Wizard applies your operations (write values and formulas, insert or delete rows and columns, delete rows that meet a condition, sort, format, column widths, find and replace, add, rename or delete sheets, freeze panes, filters) to a copy, with Excel itself when it is on this PC, and the copy appears under your answer to download, as a new attached file you can read back. Use it whenever the user asks to change, fix, clean, add to or reformat a file they attached; never answer with code or steps for them to do it. The original is never changed.

file.description: The attached workbook's label, e.g. 'F1'. Edit an edited copy (e.g. 'F2') to continue from it (pattern ^F[0-9]{1,3}$)

op.description: set: write values from cell (top-left) down and right. clear: empty a range. insert_rows / delete_rows: at row, count rows. insert_columns / delete_columns: at column (letter), count. delete_rows_where: remove every row whose column meets condition/value (header_row is the header, default 1). sort: range by column (letter or header), descending, header. format: range with bold, italic, font_color, fill, number_format, align, wrap, border. column_width: columns ('B' or 'B:D') to width, or fitted when width is omitted. find_replace: find → replace in sheet or every sheet. add_sheet: name (after). rename_sheet: sheet → name. delete_sheet. freeze: panes above and left of cell. autofilter: filter buttons on range.

sheet.description: Sheet name as the workbook shows it (may be omitted when there is one sheet; for find_replace, omit for every sheet) (0-31 characters)

values.description: set: rows of cells, e.g. [["Margin"], ["=C2-D2"]]. Numbers as digits (1234.5), formulas start with =, dates as 2026-10-23, '' empties a cell, text that looks like a number starts with '.

column.description: A column letter, or for delete_rows_where and sort the header text (0-120 characters)

value.description: delete_rows_where: the value to compare with (0-500 characters)

header.description: sort: the range's first row is a header (default true).

name.description: add_sheet / rename_sheet: the new sheet name (0-31 characters)

after.description: add_sheet: put the new sheet after this one (0-31 characters)

name.description: File name for the edited copy (default '<name> (edited)') (0-120 characters)

tools.name: wizard_query_postgresql
tools.description: Run one read-only SQL query on the company PostgreSQL server and get the rows back: joins, window functions, CTEs, any aggregation the question needs. The dataset notes describe its materialized views (what a row is, columns, units, refresh): find them with wizard_browse_knowledge (area 'datasets') or wizard_lookup_definitions and read them with wizard_read_knowledge. You can also inspect information_schema and pg_catalog. At most max_rows rows come back (truncated=true when there are more). Each call is live evidence to cite like [E3]; the user can see your SQL.

sql.description: One PostgreSQL query: SELECT ... or WITH ... SELECT .... Name tables as schema.table. It runs as a subquery, so no other statements (1-20000 characters)

database.description: Database on the server; omit for the default one. Set it when a dataset note says the view lives in another database (pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,63}$)

max_rows.description: Rows to return (hard cap 500). Aggregate in SQL rather than fetching detail rows (default 200)

tools.name: wizard_calculate
tools.description: Evaluate arithmetic exactly over named numbers (e.g. growth, ratios, per-million normalisation) instead of doing long arithmetic in your head.

expression.description: Arithmetic using + - * / ** % ( ) and abs, min, max, sum, avg, round, sqrt, e.g. '(q3 - q2) / spend_musd' (1-500 characters)

tools.name: wizard_render_visual
tools.description: Show a chart, heatmap or table in the answer. Provide the exact values, units and the evidence ids they come from; returns an id such as V1 to place in the answer. The person can copy it into PowerPoint or Excel and download it as an editable PowerPoint slide or an Excel file of its data, so never draw a chart or heatmap with text, emoji or Markdown.

kind.description: bar for ranking/comparison, line for time series, scatter for two measures, heatmap for one measure across two dimensions (markets by month, products by market: a grid of cells shaded by value, with the value in each cell), table for exact values. Never imitate a heatmap with coloured symbols in a table: use heatmap.

rows.description: One list per row, in column order. Numbers may be given as numbers or numeric text.

x.description: Column key for categories or time (charts); for a heatmap, the column naming each row (e.g. market).

series.description: Numeric column keys to plot (charts, at most 6); for a heatmap, its columns in order (e.g. one per month), all the same measure, type and unit. Leave a missing cell null: it shows as missing, never as zero.

scale.description: heatmap only: sequential (light to dark, for amounts) or diverging (around zero, for growth, change or variance: negative red, positive blue). Omit to choose by the values' signs.

evidence_ids.description: Evidence ids the values come from, e.g. ['E1','E2'].

note.description: How values were derived and any caveat (0-400 characters)

tools.name: wizard_schedule_brief
tools.description: Propose a recurring brief: a short newsletter email Metronome sends on a schedule (daily, weekly or monthly), by default to the user's own address at 08:00 Dubai time, with an Excel file of every row attached. Mirror your answer: key numbers, charts and tables, each section with its own query whose dates move with CURRENT_DATE, plus 'what moved' rules that write sentences from each run's rows. Use it when the user wants an analysis sent regularly, as soon as you know how often. It checks the schedule and the recipients, runs every query once as a test (live evidence to cite like [E3]) and shows the user the email on a card. Nothing is scheduled until the user presses Create in Metronome; the Flow then belongs to Metronome's Wizard user.

title.description: The brief's name, e.g. 'Weekly sell-out by market'. It names the email, the Metronome Flow and the Excel file (1-80 characters)

intro.description: One optional line under the title (0-200 characters)

period_sql.description: Optional query returning one text value that names the period each email covers, e.g. SELECT 'Week ' || to_char(CURRENT_DATE - 7, 'IW') AS period (0-5000 characters)

sections.description: In reading order, mirroring your answer: usually key numbers first, then the charts and tables. Each section has its own query.

kind.description: numbers: key-number tiles from the first row of the query. chart: a bar or line chart. table: the first max_rows rows (the Excel file has them all).

sql.description: One SELECT or WITH ... SELECT returning exactly what this section shows, with dates relative to CURRENT_DATE so each run covers the latest period (1-20000 characters)

label.description: The tile's label, e.g. 'Units sold' (1-40 characters)

value.description: Column with this period's value (first row of the section's query) (1-63 characters)

previous.description: Column with the period it is compared with; the tile then shows the change, e.g. ▲ 5.3% (1-63 characters)

compare.description: What the change is against, e.g. 'vs last week'. Default 'vs the previous period' (0-40 characters)

better.description: 'down' when a fall is good (costs, days of stock) (default "up")

chart.description: chart: bar (one row per category, best for markets or products) or line (one row per period, in order).

x.description: chart: the category or period column (1-63 characters)

series.description: chart: number columns. For a bar chart comparing periods, this period first, then the previous one.

change.description: bar chart with two series: show each row's percent change (default false)

columns.description: Labels and number formats for the query's columns (charts and tables); unlisted columns keep their names.

label.description: Header or legend name, e.g. 'Week 43' (0-40 characters)

max_rows.description: table: rows shown in the email (default 10)

highlights.description: 'What moved' sentences computed from this section's rows at every run.

rule.description: change: 'Units rose 5.3% to 48,210, from 45,800' (first row). largest / smallest: the row with the highest or lowest value. biggest_rise / biggest_fall: the row with the largest percent change. rose / fell: which rows went up or down ('Kuwait was the only one down: -5.5%'). above / below: rows past a threshold. record_high / record_low: the last row of a series is the highest or lowest shown. A rule with nothing to say this time (nothing fell) writes nothing.

value.description: Column with this period's value (1-63 characters)

label.description: Column naming each row, e.g. 'market'. Required except for change (1-63 characters)

previous.description: Column with the previous period's value; required for change, biggest_rise, biggest_fall, rose and fell (1-63 characters)

noun.description: What the value counts, e.g. 'units' or 'sell-out' (0-30 characters)

lead.description: Put the sentence in the 'In short' paragraph at the top instead of under its section. Lead with the two or three that matter most (default false)

database.description: Database on the server; omit for the default one (pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,63}$)

recipients.description: Only when the user names other people: their company email addresses. Omit to send it to the user's own address.

frequency.description: daily; weekly on the given days; monthly on day_of_month.

days.description: Weekly: the weekdays it is sent, e.g. ['monday'].

day_of_month.description: Monthly: the day of the month it is sent.

time.description: Only when the user gives a time: time of day on Metronome's clock, which is Dubai time, 24-hour, e.g. '07:30' (pattern ^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$; default "08:00")

subject.description: Email subject; omit to use the title (0-200 characters)

tools.name: wizard_ask_for_system
tools.description: Only when the answer needs a system that is off for this request (the person chose others, or the company uses it only when asked): name that system and why. The person gets a button under your answer to switch it on and continue. Never guess that system's data instead.

system.description: The switched-off system the answer needs: its id or name as the request's systems list gives it (e.g. gscm, ASAP) (1-60 characters)

reason.description: One short sentence for the person: what that system would add to this answer (1-300 characters)

tools.name: wizard_ask_person
tools.description: Ask the person one short question before a long route, when their answer changes where the data comes from or what the answer is (daily or weekly, which market, units or value, what a breakdown means) and nothing they said settles it. Give two to four options: they become buttons, and the one clicked is their next message. Then end your turn with the question; ask at most once per request.

question.description: One short question in the person's language, e.g. 'Daily from GSCM, or weekly from the database?' (5-300 characters)

options.description: Two to four answers the person can click, each a few words and what it costs when that differs a lot (e.g. 'Daily, from GSCM (a live read, a few minutes)'); the one you would choose first.

why.description: One short sentence: what the choice changes in the answer (0-300 characters)

tools.name: wizard_check_my_data
tools.description: Optional verification. Recompute figures you state from the cited evidence rows, check that each figure covers the period you claim, and optionally re-run cited requests to detect changed source data. Reports MATCH, DISCREPANCY, PERIOD_MISMATCH or NOT_VERIFIABLE per figure; it never edits your answer.

claims.description: Figures from your answer to recompute from cited evidence.

label.description: The statement being checked, e.g. 'EG Q3 spend' (1-160 characters)

stated_value.description: The number as stated in the answer.

evidence_id.description: For a direct figure: the evidence it comes from (pattern ^E[0-9]{1,4}$)

expression.description: For a derived figure: arithmetic over input names (0-300 characters)

period.description: Period this input should cover, e.g. 2026-Q3 or 2026-07 (pattern ^[0-9]{4}-(Q[1-4]|[0-9]{2})$)

replay_evidence_ids.description: Evidence ids whose source request should be re-run to detect changed data.

tools.name: wizard_propose_storylines
tools.description: Ask the person which story the presentation should tell, before you make it: two to four storylines the evidence supports, each with its message and its arc (the beats, in order). They become a card under your answer; the one clicked, or a story the person writes, is their next message. Use it when the person wants a presentation and has not said its story; skip it when they did. Then end your turn; it counts as your one question for this request.

question.description: The question as the person reads it, in their language (5-200 characters; default "What story should the presentation tell?")

storylines.description: Two to four different stories the evidence supports (not the same story reworded), the one you would choose first. The person picks one or writes their own.

title.description: The story's message in one line, as the deck would argue it, from what the analysis found, e.g. 'Flagship carried Q3 while Mass lost share: shift spend to the A-series' (5-140 characters)

arc.description: The beats in order, each a slide or a section, e.g. ['Q3 beat plan by 6%', 'Flagship drove it', 'Mass lost 2 pp to C-brands', 'Three moves for Q4']. At most 120 characters each.

best_for.description: Optional: the audience or moment it suits, e.g. 'a board update' or 'a planning workshop' (0-120 characters)

why.description: Optional: one short sentence on what the choice changes in the deck (0-300 characters)

tools.name: wizard_make_presentation
tools.description: Make a PowerPoint presentation from your analysis: the person gets every slide to see, download and open in PowerPoint, with editable charts and tables, in the company's design (from the knowledge base). Use it once the person has chosen the storyline (wizard_propose_storylines) or said the story themselves; render the charts and tables first with wizard_render_visual and show them by id. Every slide's title is a full-sentence takeaway that advances the storyline; the subtitle gives the scope (market, period, unit). Slide kinds and their fields: cover (title, subtitle, meta: region and date); agenda (items, or empty to list the section slides); section (title, subtitle: a divider); summary (the executive summary: points, up to 4 kpis); kpis (2-6 kpis: big figures with label, change and tone); cards (2-4 cards: numbered columns with heading, points, optional value: strategy, options, initiatives); chart (visual, chart style, up to 4 points beside it as the 'so what'); table (a table or heatmap visual, highlights: the few cells to shade good or bad, points); split (left and right panels, each a visual or points, with a heading: comparisons); text (points); closing (title: next steps or the ask, points). Any slide takes evidence_ids, a footnote and speaker notes; sources and units are written on each slide from the evidence and the visuals. Returns the deck id (D1...) to place in your answer, the outline and warnings.

title.description: The deck's title (its file name too) (1-160 characters)

storyline.description: The story the deck tells, in one or two sentences: the storyline the person chose or wrote, which every slide title advances (10-600 characters)

audience.description: Optional: who it is for, e.g. 'the CEO's monthly review' (0-120 characters)

slides.description: The slides in order, the cover first.

title.description: The slide's message as a full sentence (a takeaway, not a topic), e.g. 'Flagship carried Q3: +18% vs plan'. The cover's title is the deck's title; an agenda's defaults to 'Agenda' (0-160 characters)

subtitle.description: The scope under the title: market, period, unit, e.g. 'MENA · Q3 2026 · sell-out, units' (0-200 characters)

meta.description: cover: the line with the region and date, e.g. 'MENA · November 2026' (0-120 characters)

points.description: Bullets (summary, text, closing, beside a chart or table).

text.description: The bullet; **bold** marks a lead-in, e.g. '**Flagship:** +18% vs plan' (1-300 characters)

sub.description: Optional second-level bullets, at most 200 characters each.

kpis.description: kpis (2-6) or a summary's key figures (up to 4).

value.description: The figure as shown, e.g. '$12.4M', '+18%', '2.1 pp' (1-24 characters)

label.description: What it is, with its period and scope, e.g. 'Q3 sell-out, MENA' (1-80 characters)

change.description: Optional comparison, e.g. '▲ 6% vs plan' or '▼ 1.2 pp YoY' (0-40 characters)

tone.description: good or bad colours the change; neutral leaves it plain (default "neutral")

evidence_ids.description: Evidence the figure comes from, e.g. ['E2'].

heading.description: The card's title, e.g. 'Win the mid-tier' (1-80 characters)

text.description: The bullet; **bold** marks a lead-in, e.g. '**Flagship:** +18% vs plan' (1-300 characters)

sub.description: Optional second-level bullets, at most 200 characters each.

value.description: Optional big figure at the top of the card (0-24 characters)

visual.description: chart or table: the visual's id, e.g. 'V1' (pattern ^V[0-9]{1,4}$)

chart.description: chart: how a bar visual is drawn: column (vertical bars; time or few categories), stacked (stacked columns: a total split by channel or segment over time), percent (100% stacked columns: mix and share splits), bar (horizontal bars: rankings, long names), stacked_bar, or line (trends with markers). auto chooses.

highlights.description: table: the few cells to shade, good (green) or bad (yellow); a handful per slide, never a whole column.

row.description: The row's label, as in the visual's first column (its x) (1-120 characters)

column.description: The column's key or label (1-80 characters)

tone.description: good: the light green fill (target met, growth); bad: the light yellow fill (gap, decline).

left.description: split: the left panel (a visual or bullets, with a heading).

visual.description: A visual id from wizard_render_visual, e.g. 'V2' (pattern ^V[0-9]{1,4}$)

text.description: The bullet; **bold** marks a lead-in, e.g. '**Flagship:** +18% vs plan' (1-300 characters)

sub.description: Optional second-level bullets, at most 200 characters each.

visual.description: A visual id from wizard_render_visual, e.g. 'V2' (pattern ^V[0-9]{1,4}$)

text.description: The bullet; **bold** marks a lead-in, e.g. '**Flagship:** +18% vs plan' (1-300 characters)

sub.description: Optional second-level bullets, at most 200 characters each.

items.description: agenda: the topics; leave empty to list the deck's section slides with their pages.

evidence_ids.description: Evidence behind figures in the slide's text (a visual's evidence is added by itself).

footnote.description: An extra footnote: a definition, a caveat, how a figure was derived (0-300 characters)

notes.description: Speaker notes: what to say on this slide (0-2000 characters)

kind.description: The slide's kind; see the tool description for what each holds.

tools.name: wizard_change_presentation
tools.description: Change a presentation you made, as the person asks in the chat (a title, a slide's kind or chart style, cells to highlight, a slide added, removed or moved, the storyline): the changes make a new version the person sees in place of the old one. Read the slides first with wizard_read_presentation when you need their full content.

deck.description: The deck to change, e.g. 'D1' (its latest version is what the person sees) (pattern ^D[0-9]{1,4}$)

action.description: update: change fields of slide `at` (only the fields given in `slide`; a field set to null is removed); insert: add `slide` (a whole slide with its kind) after slide `at` (0 puts it first); delete: remove slide `at`; move: put slide `at` at number `to`; deck: change the deck's title, storyline or audience (`deck`).

at.description: The slide number, as the deck stands after the changes before this one.

slide.description: update: the fields that change, e.g. {"title": "..."} or {"kind": "table", "highlights": [...]}; insert: the whole new slide, with its kind.

subtitle.description: The scope under the title: market, period, unit, e.g. 'MENA · Q3 2026 · sell-out, units' (0-200 characters)

meta.description: cover: the line with the region and date, e.g. 'MENA · November 2026' (0-120 characters)

points.description: Bullets (summary, text, closing, beside a chart or table).

text.description: The bullet; **bold** marks a lead-in, e.g. '**Flagship:** +18% vs plan' (1-300 characters)

sub.description: Optional second-level bullets, at most 200 characters each.

kpis.description: kpis (2-6) or a summary's key figures (up to 4).

value.description: The figure as shown, e.g. '$12.4M', '+18%', '2.1 pp' (1-24 characters)

label.description: What it is, with its period and scope, e.g. 'Q3 sell-out, MENA' (1-80 characters)

change.description: Optional comparison, e.g. '▲ 6% vs plan' or '▼ 1.2 pp YoY' (0-40 characters)

evidence_ids.description: Evidence the figure comes from, e.g. ['E2'].

heading.description: The card's title, e.g. 'Win the mid-tier' (1-80 characters)

text.description: The bullet; **bold** marks a lead-in, e.g. '**Flagship:** +18% vs plan' (1-300 characters)

sub.description: Optional second-level bullets, at most 200 characters each.

value.description: Optional big figure at the top of the card (0-24 characters)

visual.description: chart or table: the visual's id, e.g. 'V1' (pattern ^V[0-9]{1,4}$)

chart.description: chart: how a bar visual is drawn: column (vertical bars; time or few categories), stacked (stacked columns: a total split by channel or segment over time), percent (100% stacked columns: mix and share splits), bar (horizontal bars: rankings, long names), stacked_bar, or line (trends with markers). auto chooses.

highlights.description: table: the few cells to shade, good (green) or bad (yellow); a handful per slide, never a whole column.

row.description: The row's label, as in the visual's first column (its x) (1-120 characters)

column.description: The column's key or label (1-80 characters)

tone.description: good: the light green fill (target met, growth); bad: the light yellow fill (gap, decline).

left.description: split: the left panel (a visual or bullets, with a heading).

visual.description: A visual id from wizard_render_visual, e.g. 'V2' (pattern ^V[0-9]{1,4}$)

text.description: The bullet; **bold** marks a lead-in, e.g. '**Flagship:** +18% vs plan' (1-300 characters)

sub.description: Optional second-level bullets, at most 200 characters each.

visual.description: A visual id from wizard_render_visual, e.g. 'V2' (pattern ^V[0-9]{1,4}$)

text.description: The bullet; **bold** marks a lead-in, e.g. '**Flagship:** +18% vs plan' (1-300 characters)

sub.description: Optional second-level bullets, at most 200 characters each.

items.description: agenda: the topics; leave empty to list the deck's section slides with their pages.

evidence_ids.description: Evidence behind figures in the slide's text (a visual's evidence is added by itself).

footnote.description: An extra footnote: a definition, a caveat, how a figure was derived (0-300 characters)

notes.description: Speaker notes: what to say on this slide (0-2000 characters)

slides.description: Slide numbers to return in full; empty: all.

tools.name: wizard_compare_evidence
tools.description: Check one of your reads against another, row by row and number by number, in Wizard's code: e.g. a portal's direct data request (portal_prove_request's first reply) against the rows the report's own screen showed for the same filters. Rows are matched by the key columns, numbers within the tolerance; the rows only one side has are listed. MATCH means everything agrees. With system and report, the outcome is kept in that report's map entry.

reference.description: What the result must equal: e.g. the rows the report's own screen showed (its grid's dataset, read after the person's path) (pattern ^E\d{1,6}$)

checked.description: The evidence to check, e.g. the first reply of portal_prove_request for the same filters (pattern ^E\d{1,6}$)

keys.description: The columns that tell one row from another on both sides, e.g. the account and the country.

reference.description: The column in the reference evidence, by name (1-200 characters)

checked.description: The same column in the evidence being checked (1-200 characters)

values.description: The numbers to compare (one pair per day for a report with a column per day).

reference.description: The column in the reference evidence, by name (1-200 characters)

checked.description: The same column in the evidence being checked (1-200 characters)

tolerance.description: The largest difference two numbers may have and still match (default 0.0)

against.description: What the reference is, in words, for the map (0-120 characters; default "the report's own screen")

system.description: With report: the portal whose map keeps the outcome, e.g. gscm (pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{1,15}$)

report.description: The report's id in that portal's map (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,79}$)

tools.name: wizard_kb_note_source
tools.description: The file of knowledge notes as it is in the knowledge base (front matter and body) with its path, to change it with wizard_kb_save_notes.

tools.name: wizard_kb_standard
tools.description: The knowledge standard: how every knowledge note is written (front matter, areas, sections, sources, status). Read it before writing or changing a note.

tools.name: wizard_kb_save_notes
tools.description: Only in a task run (Settings → Tasks): change the company's knowledge-base repository in one commit. notes adds or replaces whole notes; moves moves a note to another folder (same file name, same id) or renames it (a new file name is its new id: Wizard sets it in the note and in every other note's related); removes deletes notes no other note links to (or whose links this call removes). Every resulting note is checked against the knowledge standard first, a SIGNED note is never changed, moved or removed, and nothing is saved when anything fails.

notes.description: Notes to add or replace, whole files. A note that moves can be given here at its new path, when its text changes too.

path.description: knowledge/<area>/<note id>.md, e.g. knowledge/metrics/market-share.md. An existing note keeps its path (wizard_kb_note_source shows it); to move or rename it, use moves (pattern ^knowledge/([a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*/){0,2}[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,80}\.md$)

text.description: The whole file: front matter and body, as the knowledge standard says (20-60000 characters)

moves.description: Notes to move to another folder or rename, each by its id and its new path.

to.description: Its new path, knowledge/<area>/<id>.md. The same file name moves the note to that folder and keeps its id; another file name renames it: the file name is the new id, and Wizard sets it in the note and in every other note's related (pattern ^knowledge/([a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*/){0,2}[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,80}\.md$)

removes.description: Ids of notes to delete. Refused while another note's related names one, unless this call saves that note without the link (notes).

message.description: The commit message: what this changes and why, e.g. 'Where to get it names mapped portal reports' (5-200 characters)

tools.name: wizard_quiz_save
tools.description: Only in a task run (Settings → Tasks): publish one section of the quiz on the Cases site, the questions people answer to settle what the knowledge base is unsure of. It replaces that section's questions and leaves the other section alone. Each question says what the knowledge base holds now; people answer without signing in.

section.description: bi: Business intelligence, technical questions (data sources, reports, tables and columns, how a measure is calculated, filters, refresh times, which source to use). business: concepts, terms and acronyms, processes, organisation and strategy.

intro.description: One or two sentences shown above this section's questions, e.g. what they are about (0-400 characters; default "")

questions.description: The section's questions, the most useful first. They replace the section's questions on the site.

topic.description: A short label people scan by, e.g. 'Sell-out' or 'Fiscal weeks' (2-60 characters)

question.description: The question as people read it: one thing to answer, in plain words, ending with a question mark (10-300 characters)

now.description: What the knowledge base says now and why it is unsure (a draft, an UNKNOWN, two notes that disagree, a term with two meanings), in one or two sentences, so people can confirm or correct it (10-600 characters)

choices.description: Optional: 2 to 6 short answers to pick from (each at most 120 characters) when the plausible answers are known, e.g. from two notes that disagree. People can always write their own answer. Leave empty for an open question.

notes.description: Ids of the knowledge notes the answer would settle, e.g. ['sell-out'].

tools.name: wizard_task_files
tools.description: Only in a task that asks for a folder or file: list the files in the folder the person chose (PowerPoint, Word, Excel, email, text; subfolders included), each with an id, its path inside the folder, kind, size and date, and how many are done and left.

left.description: Only the files not marked done yet (default). False lists every file with whether it is done (default true)

find.description: Only files whose path contains these words, e.g. 'strategy' or '.potx' (0-100 characters)

offset.description: Continue the list from the next_offset you were given (default 0)

tools.name: wizard_task_read_file
tools.description: Only in a task that asks for a folder or file: read one of its files as text (slides with their charts' values, tables and speaker notes; sheets; documents), by id from wizard_task_files. The first call lists the file's parts; read a long file part by part. Returns the file's source id to cite in knowledge notes.

file.description: The file's id from wizard_task_files, e.g. 'f3a9c21b0' (pattern ^f[0-9a-f]{8}$)

part.description: Only this part, e.g. 'Slide 4' or 'Sheet: Sales' (names come back in 'parts'). Omit to read from the start (0-120 characters)

offset.description: Continue a long file from the next_offset you were given (default 0)

tools.name: wizard_task_design
tools.description: Only in a task that asks for a folder or file: how up to 4 presentations look, read by PowerPoint: slide size, the theme's colors and fonts, the master's title and body styles, the layouts and how often each is used, what is on every slide (logo, footer, confidentiality label, page number), fonts, sizes and colors used, fills, charts, tables, pictures, words per slide and the outline of slide titles; plus what every presentation read so far shares.

files.description: Ids of up to 4 presentations from wizard_task_files.

tools.name: wizard_task_compare
tools.description: Only in a task that asks for a file: check Wizard's evidence (a portal reply, a query) against the person's own export, row by row and number by number: rows matched by the key columns, numbers within a tolerance, and the rows only one side has. MATCH means every row and number agrees. With system and report, the outcome is kept in that report's map entry.

file.description: The person's file (a spreadsheet or CSV) from wizard_task_files (pattern ^f[0-9a-f]{8}$)

sheet.description: Its sheet, when it has several (0-120 characters)

evidence_id.description: The evidence to check, e.g. the first reply of portal_prove_request (pattern ^E\d{1,6}$)

keys.description: The columns that tell one row from another on both sides, e.g. the account, the country and the date.

file.description: The column in the person's file: its header as the sheet shows it, or its key (1-200 characters)

wizard.description: The same column in Wizard's evidence, by name (1-200 characters)

values.description: The numbers to compare, file column against Wizard column (one pair per day for a report with a column per day).

file.description: The column in the person's file: its header as the sheet shows it, or its key (1-200 characters)

wizard.description: The same column in Wizard's evidence, by name (1-200 characters)

tolerance.description: The largest difference two numbers may have and still match (rounding on screen) (default 0.5)

system.description: With report: the portal whose map keeps the outcome, e.g. gscm (pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{1,15}$)

report.description: The report's id in that portal's map (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,79}$)

tools.name: wizard_task_files_done
tools.description: Only in a task that asks for a folder: mark files done once what they hold is saved in the knowledge base (or they hold nothing to keep), so the next round of the task skips them.

files.description: Ids of the files whose content is now saved in the knowledge base, or that hold nothing to keep.

note.description: What was taken from them, or why nothing was (e.g. 'only pictures', 'duplicate of f1a2b3c4d') (0-300 characters)

tools.name: portal_guide
tools.description: How a company portal (ASAP, GSCM, the Big Data Portal: its information catalog, where tables are found, and Superset, where they are queried) works and how to read it with portal_run: its applications and addresses, its structure, where its data really comes from, the background data requests to call instead of clicking, the W.* JavaScript helpers, pitfalls, and the scripts saved for it on this PC. Read it before writing steps for a portal.

tools.name: portal_run
tools.description: Read a company portal live, in the person's own signed-in Wizard browser (Chrome, in the background): your own steps (open pages, click, fill, wait, look around, read tables) and JavaScript evaluated in the page, where W.* helpers read Nexacro datasets, walk ASAP's menu, replay the portal's own data requests (W.requests, W.replay), search the Big Data Portal's information catalog and query Superset, and request steps that send a portal's data request straight from the browser with the person's session. Prefer the portal's data requests over clicking through screens, and the map's (portal_map) routes and saved scripts over exploring. Everything a step reads is recorded as evidence with an id such as E3 (a table, a {columns, rows} object or a list of objects, as its rows; anything else as key/value rows): cite it next to its numbers and lists. The result also lists the data requests the page made, with secrets removed. Wizard refuses saves, deletes, submissions, uploads, access requests, sign-outs and other hosts.

system.description: The portal: asap, gscm or bdp (portal_guide lists the ones this person has) (pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{1,15}$)

steps.description: The steps to run, in order. Omit when running a saved script.

action.description: goto: open url (a path on the portal, or a portal address). click / fill / select: the element named by selector, role (+ name) or text; fill and select take value. press: a key (value, e.g. Enter). wait: for the element to be visible (or value 'hidden'), or value 'load'/'networkidle', or timeout_ms alone. evaluate: run script, JavaScript in the page (an async function body ending in return; W helpers and P parameters are defined). read_table: an HTML table as rows (selector, default the first table). look: the page's controls, tables, frames and text, to explore. back: browser back. use_page: switch to open page number nth (popups). request: send one data request (url, method, body, headers) straight from the browser with the person's session cookies, without opening or waiting for a page: the fastest way to call a portal route the map knows. The reply is parsed (Nexacro SSV or XML, JSON); a reply with one dataset comes back as a table, else give script, a JavaScript body that gets R = {status, contentType, text, data} and returns a table.

url.description: goto / request: '/path?query' on the portal application the page is on, or a full portal address (portal_guide lists them; the Big Data Portal's information catalog and Superset have one each) (0-4000 characters)

reload.description: goto: open the address even when the browser is already on it with GSCM's client running (Wizard keeps that page otherwise: a reload restarts the client and its sign-in, a minute or more). Only for a stuck client.

method.description: request: the HTTP method (default POST with a body, else GET).

body.description: request: the request body exactly as the portal sends it (a Nexacro SSV or XML body, form fields, JSON); {{name}} parameters are filled in (0-200000 characters)

headers.description: request: headers the route needs, such as Content-Type (cookies are the browser's own).

role.description: ARIA role, e.g. button, link, tab, menuitem, option (0-40 characters)

text.description: Exact visible text of the element (0-200 characters)

frame.description: Frame name (e.g. content-frame) or part of its address; default the page itself (0-200 characters)

nth.description: Which match when several elements match (0 = first); for use_page, the page number.

value.description: Text to fill, option to select, key to press, or the wait condition (0-2000 characters)

script.description: evaluate: JavaScript body, e.g. 'const d = W.nexacro.read("ds_list"); return d;'. request: what to return from the reply R, e.g. 'return R.data.datasets.ds_out;'. Return a table as {columns, rows} or a list of objects to cite it (0-30000 characters)

limit.description: look: how many controls to list (default 60).

save_as.description: A short name for this step's result (0-60 characters)

script.description: Run a script saved earlier with portal_save_script instead of steps (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,59}$)

name.description: Parameter name, used as P.name in scripts and {{name}} in other fields (pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$)

title.description: What this reads, in business words, e.g. 'GSCM weekly sell-out by market, W40'. Names the evidence (0-160 characters)

max_rows.description: Rows of each table returned to you (all rows are counted) (default 200)

tools.description: Keep steps that worked as a named script for this person's portal, with parameters, so a later question runs it with portal_run(script=...) instead of exploring again. Saves on this PC only; it changes nothing in the portal.

description.description: What it returns and when to use it (10-600 characters)

The reply is parsed (Nexacro SSV or XML, JSON); a reply with one dataset comes back as a table, else give script, a JavaScript body that gets R = {status, contentType, text, data} and returns a table.

reload.description: goto: open the address even when the browser is already on it with GSCM's client running (Wizard keeps that page otherwise: a reload restarts the client and its sign-in, a minute or more). Only for a stuck client.

method.description: request: the HTTP method (default POST with a body, else GET).

body.description: request: the request body exactly as the portal sends it (a Nexacro SSV or XML body, form fields, JSON); {{name}} parameters are filled in (0-200000 characters)

save_as.description: A short name for this step's result (0-60 characters)

params.description: Parameters with an example value each.

tools.name: portal_map
tools.description: The map Wizard keeps of a company portal (GSCM, ASAP, the Big Data Portal): what Gemini learned exploring it. Without arguments: how the portal works, its proven shortcuts, and the index of mapped reports. find: the reports that match business words, in full: what each is for (use_for) and not for (not_for, with the report to use instead), the knowledge notes defining its terms, menu path and id, how to open it fastest, its filters and their values, the datasets and columns, and the data requests that return its rows with the filters as parameters. Read it before exploring a portal: a mapped report is read in one portal_run.

system.description: The portal: asap, gscm or bdp (pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{1,15}$)

find.description: Business words or a report name: returns the best matching reports in full (0-300 characters)

report.description: One report's id or menu id: returns it in full (0-120 characters)

topic.description: One topic's id: returns its full text (0-80 characters)

todo.description: True: the reports still to map (todo, partial, failed), for exploring, the mapped reports whose options beyond the default view are still to explore (to_configure), and the mapped reports still to route (portal_map_route) (default false)

tools.name: portal_map_save
tools.description: Add what you learned about a portal to its map, so later questions go straight to the data: the overview, topics (technical details and shortcuts you proved), and reports by id (menu path and id, a business summary, what it is for and not for, how to open it, filters and their values, datasets and columns, data requests with {{param}} placeholders, status). Only the fields you give change. Metadata only: never data rows or secrets. Saved on this PC and published to the knowledge base when this PC can write to it; it changes nothing in the portal.

overview.description: How the portal works as a whole (replaces the old overview): the client, frames, sign-in and session, how menus and reports open, the data request format, waits and popups (0-30000 characters)

topics.description: Technical details and shortcuts, added or updated by id.

id.description: Short stable id, e.g. open-report-by-menu-id, transactions, weeks (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,79}$)

text.description: What a later script needs: how it works, the exact calls, selectors, routes and formats, and the steps or JavaScript that proved it (10-200000 characters)

reports.description: Reports added or updated by id; only the fields you give change.

use_for.description: 2-5 short phrases: the business questions and terms the report answers, in the words people use, with the acronyms in its name (e.g. 'MS' = market share): 'shipment market share by vendor', 'foldable share by price tier'.

not_for.description: Near misses, above all a report that measures the same term differently (retail panel share vs shipment share, sell-in vs sell-out, plan vs actual).

question.description: A question this report looks right for but must not answer, e.g. 'retail sell-out share' (3-300 characters)

use_instead.description: The report that does answer it: its id in this map, or 'portal:id' for another portal's map. Leave it out when no mapped report does (pattern ^([a-z][a-z0-9]{1,15}:)?[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,79}$)

definitions.description: Ids of the knowledge notes that define its terms (wizard_lookup_definitions / wizard_browse_knowledge), e.g. 'market-share'.

id.description: Stable id: the menu id or a short kebab-case name, e.g. as470 or weekly-sellout (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,79}$)

status.description: todo: listed, not mapped yet. mapped: open, filters, data, every option beyond the default view (views) and a proven fast route are known. partial: some of it. failed / skipped: say why in notes.

summary.description: What the report shows in business words: measures, grain, period, units (0-3000 characters)

open.description: The fastest proven way to open it (a call, steps or JavaScript), and how to tell it has loaded. In GSCM, one evaluate step without a goto: await W.nexacro.open('<the client's open function>', '<menu id>') (0-6000 characters)

name.description: The filter's label on screen, e.g. Week, Market, Plan version (0-160 characters)

component.description: Its component path or selector (0-400 characters)

kind.description: Combo, MultiCombo, Calendar, Edit, Radio, CheckBox, popup (0-60 characters)

values.description: Its options (code = label, every one of them) or format (e.g. YYYYWW, Sunday-start weeks), and where the options come from (an inner dataset, a lookup request) (0-200000 characters)

param.description: The request parameter or body field this filter sets (0-120 characters)

dataset.description: The dataset name, e.g. ds_list (0-160 characters)

component.description: The grid (or chart) showing it (0-400 characters)

labels.description: Column ids with their screen headers and units, e.g. QTY = Sell-out units (0-200000 characters)

views.description: Every option beyond the default view: the configuration gear's column chooser, view, grouping, measure and unit switches, with every choice and what it adds. An empty list says the report has none (explored); leaving it out means it was not explored yet.

name.description: The option as the screen names it: the grid's gear / Configuration (column chooser), a view or grouping switch, a measure or unit toggle, a layout tab (0-160 characters)

component.description: How to reach it: the control's component path, and the dialog it opens (0-400 characters)

path.description: The clicks from the open report to this choice, with the labels exactly as the screen shows them, e.g. 'Configuration > Sales > Sales > ORG Sales, then Apply' (0-600 characters)

requires.description: What must be set before the choice works, and what the portal says otherwise, e.g. 'subsidiaries chosen one by one in the search area (all of them is fine; a region such as Middle East is refused: "cannot select so much granularity")' (0-2000 characters)

options.description: Every choice it offers (each selectable column, grouping, measure...), the default ones marked, e.g. 'OrgSales (account), Country, Model (default off); Region (default on)' (0-200000 characters)

columns.description: The column ids the non-default choices add to the dataset, e.g. orgsales.

effect.description: What choosing it changes, as proved: a new request parameter (name and values), another dataset or route, or only columns the dataset already had; and whether the choice stays saved for the person (0-50000 characters)

how.description: The proven steps or request that read the report with these choices (e.g. open the gear, tick OrgSales, Apply, search; or the request with its parameter) (0-50000 characters)

name.description: What it does, e.g. search, combo-markets (0-120 characters)

url.description: The route, as a path on the portal (e.g. /gscm/xyz/selectList.do) (0-2000 characters)

body.description: The body with the filter values as {{param}} placeholders, otherwise exactly as captured (0-200000 characters)

params.description: The {{param}} names in url and body, each matching a filter's param.

reply.description: What comes back: dataset names, columns, paging (0-2000 characters)

verified.description: Ignored here: only portal_prove_request marks a request verified, after Wizard itself sent it twice (default false)

script.description: A saved script (portal_save_script) that reads it with parameters (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,59}$)

notes.description: Pitfalls: waits, popups, paging, limits, why it failed (0-50000 characters)

remove.description: Report ids to drop (duplicates, entries that are not reports).

note.description: One line for the map's log: what this save adds (0-600 characters)

tools.name: portal_prove_request
tools.description: Prove a report's data request: Wizard sends it twice from the person's browser, with the values given (first) and with one changed (second), and keeps it in the map as proven only when both answers are clean (no error from the portal), hold the same datasets and columns, and the changed value changed the rows. Only this marks a request verified, and a report is mapped only once one of its requests is proven. Each reply is evidence to cite and to check against the person's own export. Same read-only rules as portal_run.

system.description: The portal: asap, gscm or bdp (pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{1,15}$)

report.description: The report's id in the map, e.g. db4009 (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,79}$)

name.description: What it does, e.g. search, combo-markets (0-120 characters)

url.description: The route, as a path on the portal (e.g. /gscm/xyz/selectList.do) (0-2000 characters)

body.description: The body with the filter values as {{param}} placeholders, otherwise exactly as captured (0-200000 characters)

params.description: The {{param}} names in url and body, each matching a filter's param.

reply.description: What comes back: dataset names, columns, paging (0-2000 characters)

verified.description: Ignored here: only portal_prove_request marks a request verified, after Wizard itself sent it twice (default false)

first.description: Values for every {{param}}: the ones the screen used (or the person's own export).

name.description: Parameter name, used as P.name in scripts and {{name}} in other fields (pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$)

second.description: The same values with one changed, e.g. the date one day earlier or another subsidiary.

name.description: Parameter name, used as P.name in scripts and {{name}} in other fields (pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$)

tools.name: portal_map_route
tools.description: Say what reports already in a portal's map are for: use_for (the business questions and terms each answers), not_for (near misses, with the report to use instead) and definitions (the knowledge notes for its terms), plus a business summary where a report has none. It changes nothing else: not the menu path, how to open it, filters, data, requests, script or status, and it adds or removes no report. Use it for the reports portal_map(todo=true) lists under to_route.

reports.description: Reports already in the map, each with its routing; what you give replaces its earlier routing.

use_for.description: 2-5 short phrases: the business questions and terms the report answers, in the words people use, with the acronyms in its name (e.g. 'MS' = market share): 'shipment market share by vendor', 'foldable share by price tier'.

not_for.description: Near misses, above all a report that measures the same term differently (retail panel share vs shipment share, sell-in vs sell-out, plan vs actual).

question.description: A question this report looks right for but must not answer, e.g. 'retail sell-out share' (3-300 characters)

use_instead.description: The report that does answer it: its id in this map, or 'portal:id' for another portal's map. Leave it out when no mapped report does (pattern ^([a-z][a-z0-9]{1,15}:)?[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,79}$)

definitions.description: Ids of the knowledge notes that define its terms (wizard_lookup_definitions / wizard_browse_knowledge), e.g. 'market-share'.

id.description: The id of a report already in the map (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,79}$)

summary.description: What the report shows in business words: measures, grain, period, units. Kept only when the report has no summary yet (0-3000 characters)

routing_note.description: Only when the map says too little to tell what the report is for: what is missing (0-600 characters)

note.description: One line for the map's log (0-600 characters)

tools.name: wizard_dashboards
tools.description: List the team's dashboards (the Dashboards system): standalone HTML pages that combine the company database's data with the team's business logic (definitions, filters, adjustments). Each with an id, title, the date its figures are as of (stated on the page, else the file's modified time), size and subfolder. Optional find words match titles, subfolders, file names and headings.

find.description: Words to look for in titles, subfolders, file names and headings, e.g. 'weekly sell out'. Omit to list every dashboard (0-200 characters)

offset.description: Continue the list from the next_offset you were given (default 0)

tools.name: wizard_read_dashboard
tools.description: Read one dashboard as data, by id from wizard_dashboards: title, as-of date, headings and visible text, its tables as rows and the data in its scripts (chart series and data arrays, as Plotly, ECharts, Chart.js, Highcharts or Vega charts hold them) with chart and axis titles. The first read is an overview with the first rows of each part; read a part (text, T2, D1 or a heading) with part, and continue with offset. Each part read is evidence to cite like [E3] (LIVE: the dashboard as it is, as of the date it states). Wizard never runs the page's scripts or fetches what it loads, and says what it could not read.

dashboard.description: The dashboard's id from wizard_dashboards, e.g. 'd1a2b3c4d5e', or its path inside the folder, e.g. 'Sales/weekly.html' (1-300 characters)

part.description: Omit for the overview (title, as-of, headings, the start of the text and the first rows of each table and data set). Or one part: 'text', a table or data set such as 'T2' or 'D1', or a heading's words for the text under it (0-120 characters)

offset.description: Continue a part from the next_offset you were given (characters of text, or rows) (default 0)

tools.name: nerp_list_views
tools.description: List NERP's views (the only things in NERP you can query), with each view's dataset note when one maps it: what a row is, its columns' meaning and the filters that keep a query fast. Give find to rank them by business words.

find.description: Business words or part of a view's name; leave it out to list every view (0-200 characters)

tools.name: nerp_view_columns
tools.description: One NERP view's columns and types as the database has them, and its dataset note.

view.description: The view's name, as nerp_list_views gives it (1-200 characters)

tools.name: nerp_query
tools.description: Run one read-only SELECT on NERP's views and get the rows back: joins, CTEs, any aggregation. It may name only NERP's views (nerp_list_views); a table, another schema or the catalog is refused. The views can be very large: read the view's dataset note first and filter as it says. Each call is live evidence to cite like [E3]; the user can see your SQL.

sql.description: One SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT) that names only NERP's views, unqualified or as <schema>.<view>. Aggregate and filter in SQL: the views can be very large (1-20000 characters)

max_rows.description: Rows to return (truncated=true when there are more) (default 200)
